name: Dancer
description: Dancer by Helene Brox catches a cream figure mid-stride on a sky blue ground, arms rippling like ribbons caught in their own momentum. There is no face and no floor, just the shape of movement itself, one arm curling back while the other reaches high, painted with the loose confidence of a paper cut-out. It reads clearly from right across a room, and it brings genuine motion to a calm one.

name: Dragon
description: Dragon by Helene Brox coils across a black ground in ribbons of white, red, pink and grey, a beast glimpsed in fragments rather than drawn whole. Find the pale blue eyes and the composition snaps into focus; relax, and it dissolves back into pure rhythm. The most energetic piece in Brox's collection sits closer to pattern than portrait, and the black ground gives every colour real bite. One for a wall that can hold its nerve.

name: Eltsjoen
description: Eltsjoen by Ingunn Dybendal reimagines a Nordic lake landscape as dense coloured-pencil pattern: pink sky, dark mountain, patterned forest, blue water. Every band of the scene becomes ornament: clouds stretched into ribbons, trees turned to folk motifs, the water pooling in pale rings around a bridge. It is the most detailed piece in the gallery, drawn stroke by stroke, and it rewards the hundredth look as much as the first.

name: Eye Nose Eye
description: Eye Nose Eye by Simen Wahlqvist turns a face into a Venn diagram: two overlapping circles labelled eye and eye, and where they meet, nose. A bald cream head on a near-black ground wears the diagram as spectacles, yellow and red circles meeting in blue. Wahlqvist works in as few lines as possible and reckons a drawing is done when it makes him laugh; this one clearly qualified. Dry, tidy and quietly ridiculous.

name: Half Man
description: Half Man by Simen Wahlqvist splits a pink figure clean in two on a bright green ground, the torso arching over backwards while the legs stand firm. The head hovers in the gap between the halves, wearing an expression somewhere between effort and mild complaint. It is drawn with Wahlqvist's usual economy, a handful of lines and two colours doing all the work, and it makes an absurd, deadpan anchor for a hallway or desk wall.

name: Hummer og Vin
description: Hummer og Vin by Sia Siamos looks straight down on a summer table: a whole lobster on a blue platter, lemons, vine tomatoes and glasses of red wine. Hands reach in from the edges, candles lean at friendly angles, and grapes and carrots crowd the green cloth, all painted loose enough that the scene feels mid-conversation. The title is Norwegian for lobster and wine, and the print keeps exactly that promise: a long, generous evening, held mid-toast.

name: Hyttefrokost
description: Hyttefrokost by Sia Siamos piles ripe tomatoes, grapes and a carafe of water against green kitchen tiles, drawn in bold, joyful colour. The title means cabin breakfast in Norwegian, and the drawing has that holiday ease: big tomatoes heaped on a striped board, cherry tomatoes scattering across a lilac table, a yellow checked cloth thrown down rather than laid. Every outline is quick and confident, closer to a sketchbook page than a formal still life.

name: IThinkIThink
description: IThinkIThink by Helene Brox spells out its confession, I think I think too much, in green brush strokes across a cobalt head on shocking pink. Red squiggles loop through the profile like thoughts refusing to settle, and two wide, mismatched eyes complete the picture of a brain at full volume. The loudest print in the gallery, and the most instantly likeable; buy it for the person whose mind never sits down, even if that person is you.

name: Mean Snothing
description: Mean Snothing by Simen Wahlqvist gives an orange man a Newton's cradle for eyes, one ball caught mid-swing, on a flat green ground. The face underneath stays perfectly deadpan, which is the whole joke: physics happening on a forehead and nobody reacting. Drawn in Wahlqvist's spare, confident line, it is the kind of print that gets a second look from every guest, and it earns its place in a home office better than any motivational poster.

name: Morgenlevering
description: Morgenlevering by Sia Siamos paints a breakfast table in full swing: cafetière coffee, croissants on a checked cloth, pink carnations in a red vase. Morning light falls through the window onto a warm terracotta table crowded with cups, sliced bread and a water carafe, everything tilted towards you as if you have just pulled up a chair. The name translates as morning delivery, which is about right: the whole table feels newly arrived.

name: Morgenstrekk
description: Morgenstrekk by Simen Wahlqvist catches the day's first full-body stretch, a figure reaching for a small sun with a charging cable wound around him. The cable trails down to a plug at the skirting board, as though he has just unplugged himself from the night and is charging off the morning instead. Ochre on warm peach, drawn in Wahlqvist's handful of lines, it is the gentlest and most optimistic of his prints.

name: Slingshot
description: Slingshot by Simen Wahlqvist strings elastic between two raised fingers and loads a small, contented figure into the palm below, ready to fly. A peace sign turned catapult, drawn in white on a bright tomato red ground with the fewest lines the joke will allow. The figure looks entirely relaxed about what happens next, which is somehow the funniest part. A square print with a proper glint in its eye.

name: Swallow Dive
description: Swallow Dive by Helene Brox fills the frame edge to edge with diving birds in deep cobalt, bold cut-out shapes swooping over warm cream. There is no horizon and no resting point, just the repeated plunge of wings that turns a flock into pattern. The two-colour discipline is what makes it: one blue, one cream, and all the movement carried by shape alone. Calm enough for a bedroom, confident enough for the room where guests land.

name: Tree Top Peach
description: Tree Top Peach by Helene Brox weaves branches and perched birds into a soft peach lattice, papercut style, inside its own drawn border. Look longer and the birds keep arriving: dozens of small silhouettes tucked among the tangle, all in a single warm tone on cream. It is the gentlest print in the gallery, closer to folk papercut than illustration, and it settles a bedroom or reading corner without disappearing into it.

name: Trysilkaffe
description: Trysilkaffe by Ingunn Dybendal crams a green mug with an impossible bouquet, folk flowers in red, purple and teal above a diamond-check cloth. Every bloom is a different invention, daisies, rosettes and seed heads drawn petal by petal in coloured pencil, and even the mug carries its own tulip motif. It is pattern on pattern on pattern, cheerfully too much in the best Nordic folk tradition, and it wakes up any wall it hangs on.

name: Vinkveld
description: Vinkveld by Sia Siamos paints a wine evening in thick, glossy strokes: a glass of red, green olives, dark grapes and vine tomatoes against checked tiles. A bottle stands in the foreground with the cork already adrift, which tells you where the evening is heading. Vinkveld means wine evening, and the brushwork agrees, thicker and moodier than Siamos's other table scenes, with the checked tiles dissolving into loose strokes behind. One for a kitchen or dining wall.

name: Sunday Brunch
description: Sunday Brunch by Hedvig Wallin lays a breakfast table in pastel: yoghurt with berries, croissants, cucumber sandwiches and a cup of coffee on a blue cloth. Seen from above, the table curves against green kitchen tiles and a pink wall, with a jar of jam, a halved grapefruit and a bunch of cut flowers crowding the edges. Drawn in ink and watercolour with a deliberately wonky perspective, it has the loose, handmade warmth of a morning nobody is rushing, and the more you look, the more turns up on the table.

name: Rosa Blomster
description: Rosa Blomster by Hedvig Wallin fills a glass vase with a bouquet in pinks and reds, set against a wall of soft pink tiles. The title is Swedish for pink flowers, and that is the whole idea: dahlias, buds and striped leaves drawn in ink over watercolour, every petal its own careful shape, with the stems showing through the water. It is a simple way to bring real colour into a room, and it sits as happily in a bedroom as it does in a kitchen.

name: Massa Äpplen
description: Massa Äpplen by Hedvig Wallin lines up row upon row of small watercolour apples in reds, greens and everything between, each finished with a stroke of ink. The title is Swedish for lots of apples, and the pleasure is in the repetition: no two are the same shape or colour, so a grid that reads as pattern from across the room becomes a hundred little portraits up close. Made for a kitchen or dining wall, where it hangs like a well-stocked fruit bowl.

name: Small House Big Ocean
description: Small House Big Ocean by Hedvig Wallin sets a little house on a rock in the middle of a sea of rolling waves, drawn entirely in black ink line. Every wave is built from patient parallel strokes, so a stormy subject ends up oddly calm, and the eye keeps returning to the one door and its handful of windows. It is a line drawing that suits a child’s room as well as a living room, and it hangs well beside anything with colour in it.

name: Cruise
description: Cruise by Mikko Saarainen sails a liner through green waves, with a saluting captain, a girl whose plaits stream out behind her and a leaping fish. Orange birds wheel around the funnel, a boy in a woolly hat aims a yellow camera at the water, and every passenger has spotted something different. Drawn in a bold line and flat, faintly grainy colour in teal, orange and yellow, it has the cheerful overload of a holiday photograph where nobody is looking at the lens.

name: Family Trip
description: Family Trip by Mikko Saarainen loads an orange car past the roofline: suitcases, a picnic basket, a rolled rug and a mouse on the roof rack. Inside, a yellow dog grins out of one window and a green cat hangs out of another, with four children and a driver in glasses squeezed in between, a bird on the aerial and exhaust puffing behind. Drawn in a bold black line over flat colour, it is the whole chaotic business of leaving on holiday in a single square.

name: Journey
description: Journey by Mikko Saarainen takes a red car over a stone bridge below snow-capped mountains, through autumn trees in orange and yellow. It is the quietest of his prints and the most graphic: big rolling clouds, flowering shrubs crowding the foreground, two birds up in the pines, and the arch of the bridge repeated in its own reflection. The muted palette and flat shapes owe something to the old railway travel posters, and it is calm enough to hold a wall on its own.

name: URF!
description: URF! by Mikko Saarainen is a whole comic page in one print: a knight in blue armour losing an argument with a green dragon, across three panels. He is blasted off a wall in the first, swinging a sword at the dragon's tail in the second, and down to a fire extinguisher by the third, while another knight creeps through a ruin towards a red door. Autumn trees and grey castle stone fill every gap, and there is a joke in almost all of them.

name: Stockholm
description: Stockholm's rooftops, towers and waterfront gather in a colourful illustration by Ishtar Bäcklund Dakhil. Orange brick, yellow façades and green spires rise above two boats, with pale blue sky keeping the busy scene open. Look closer for rows of windows, flowering trees and the small architectural details that make the city feel lived in. A print of Ishtar's hand-painted original.

name: Frukt & Grönt
description: Fruit, vegetables and handwritten Swedish labels fill Frukt & Grönt by Ishtar Bäcklund Dakhil. A deep purple aubergine sits above pineapple, sweetcorn, leafy greens and bright red tomatoes, with roots and stems threading through the white spaces. It's a generous, detailed gathering of everyday ingredients, with something new to spot each time you pass. A print of Ishtar's hand-painted original.

name: Desert Circles
description: Overlapping white circles divide a desert landscape into curved fragments in this artwork by Ishtar Bäcklund Dakhil. Rust-coloured rocks, cacti and dusty pink hills repeat inside the pattern, interrupted by bright turquoise openings. The repeated shapes draw your eye towards the centre, while the scattered marks and uneven colour keep each section different. A print of Ishtar's hand-painted original.

name: Month of May
description: Lilac flowers, bees and pale circles surround a fine geometric star in Month of May, an artwork by Ishtar Bäcklund Dakhil. Purple blossoms spill across the edges, with green leaves, yellow flowers and smaller plants gathering below. Repeating curves draw these garden details into a central pattern, set against a soft pink sky and muted blue ground. A print of Ishtar's hand-painted original.

name: Flight Over the Valley
description: A pale aeroplane with a row of windows glides over a green valley in this illustration by Ishtar Bäcklund Dakhil, a spread from her children's book. Its wings stretch across winding blue rivers, pink rock faces and thick vegetation. The white shape stands out against the busy landscape below, and can also be read as a bird in flight. A print of Ishtar's hand-painted original.

name: Creature Among Blue Leaves
description: A pale horned creature peers through layers of blue leaves in this illustration by Ishtar Bäcklund Dakhil. Broad fans and pointed fronds fill the dark background, partly hiding its spotted face and curved horns. Small touches of ochre interrupt the cool palette, while the overlapping plants make the creature feel tucked inside its own world. A print of Ishtar's hand-painted original.

name: Surfer with Orange Sun
description: A surfer balances above a turquoise wave with a bright orange sun behind her in this illustration by Ishtar Bäcklund Dakhil. Outstretched arms and a bent knee give the figure a light, poised movement. Dark clothing makes a strong shape against the sun, while white foam breaks across the lower part of the picture. A print of Ishtar's hand-painted original.

name: Through the Willows
description: A river glows gold beneath a screen of willow and oak leaves, with a single bird cutting across the haze. Soft, warm light and a quiet, waiting stillness.

name: Pines Under Starlight
description: Snow-laden pines stand still beneath a clear, star-scattered sky. A hushed, cold-clear winter night.

name: Boathouses in winter
description: A lit window and a lone streetlamp cut through a dark, snow-heavy night beside the boathouses. Falling snow catches the light; everything else stays in shadow.

name: Frozen currents
description: Pale ridges of ice swirl across dark water, dusted with fresh snow, closer to a painting than a photograph. An abstract, almost weightless study in movement and cold.

name: The Road at Sunset
description: A small group of cyclists ride a curving road into low evening sun, forest and hills fading into the haze beyond. A warm, quiet end to the day, caught mid-journey.

name: Sun Over the Forest
description: A huge, hazy sun hangs low over a dark line of trees, the sky burning orange around it. Simple, elemental, and quietly dramatic.

name: Swan on Still Water
description: A lone swan drifts across a misty lake at first light, reeds standing dark in the foreground. Calm, hushed, and completely still.

name: Morning, Cabin Room
description: Soft light falls through lace curtains onto a simple bed, with greenery pressing close against the window. A quiet, unmade corner of a wooden cabin.

name: Path Through the Trees
description: A wooden boardwalk winds through dense, shadowed forest towards a bright clearing ahead. The kind of path that pulls you on to see what's next.

name: Sheep on the Track
description: A small flock of dark sheep stands watching on a muddy track between hedgerows, a green pasture opening beyond them. Damp, overcast, and entirely rural.

name: Fitting in
description: A piece that reflects on gender, the body and the relationship between individual human experience and the public expectation to fit into a certain frame. Drawn in a bold black line, a figure in a dress is built from a tangle of bodies, set on a field of pink.

name: Precautions
description: An illustration that invites you to question both the innocence of a guinea pig and the precautions taken around it. A small guinea pig sits inside a spiked collar, drawn in fine blue hatching on white.

name: Pressure
description: An illustration of a person with a very big clothes peg on their head, or a visual representation of a psychological experience. Drawn in a clean black line on white.

name: Good conversation
description: A take on what unconstructive communication feels like. Two strained faces, each running inside a wheel of its own, are stacked into a figure of eight on a bright yellow ground.
